label: CHANCE_1, incidental: the giving varies along with some other being's role as a condition
definition: IncidentalVariationAt F A w y: y exists at w, and at some world v accessible from w where y exists, y's giving differs (not GivingSameIn F y w v) and some being z distinct from y is an external condition of y's giving at one of w, v and not at the other.
note: Analyst definition, attribution deferred (docs/notes/will-versus-chance.md). A surrogate for Aristotle's chance (Physics II.5-6, navigation): it types only a necessary condition of incidental causation (a varying concurring cause); 'for the sake of something' and 'not always or for the most part' are not typed. Example: a debt repaid because the creditor happened to go to the market. Excluded at an invariant set-up (Model.Laws 1). Aquinas's chance is of this per accidens kind.
